verses.zh: 雅各举目观看，见以扫来了，后头跟着四百人，他就把孩子们分开交给利亚、拉结，和两个使女，
verses.en: Jacob looked up[NOTE:1] and saw that Esau was coming[NOTE:2] along with 400 men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants.
notes: Heb “and Jacob lifted up his eyes.”
Or “and look, Esau was coming.” By the use of the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), the narrator invites the reader to view the scene through Jacob’s eyes.

verses.zh: 并且叫两个使女和她们的孩子在前头，利亚和她的孩子在后头，拉结和约瑟在尽后头。
verses.en: He put the servants and their children in front, with Leah and her children behind them, and Rachel and Joseph behind them.[NOTE:1]
notes: This kind of ranking according to favoritism no doubt fed the jealousy over Joseph that later becomes an important element in the narrative. It must have been painful to the family to see that they were expendable.
verses.commentary:
33:2 Notice the distinction in the family. The lesser wives and children go first, his favorites go
last (i.e., Rachel and Joseph). Things have changed in Jacob's heart, however, and he goes before them all
(cf. Gen. 33:3). If they are to be killed, he will be killed first. He still strategizes, but he now trusts in
YHWH's presence and promised protection.

verses.zh: 他自己在他们前头过去，一连七次俯伏在地才就近他哥哥。
verses.en: But Jacob[NOTE:1] himself went on ahead of them, and he bowed toward the ground seven times as he approached[NOTE:2] his brother.
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (Jacob) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “until his drawing near unto his brother.” The construction uses the preposition with the infinitive construct to express a temporal clause.
verses.commentary:
33:3 "bowed down" This VERB (BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel IMPERFECT
with waw) is repeated four times.

- Jacob bows before Esau, Gen. 33:3

- the maids and their children bow before Esau, Gen. 33:6

- Leah and her children bow before Esau, Gen. 33:7

- Rachel and her child bow before Esau, Gen. 33:7

▣ "seven times" This was a gesture of submission (i.e., El Amarna Letters, 14th century
B.C.).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS
IN SCRIPTURE, #4

verses.zh: 以扫跑来迎接他，将他抱住，又搂着他的颈项，与他亲嘴，两个人就哭了。
verses.en: But Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, hugged his neck, and kissed him. Then they both wept.
verses.commentary:
33:4 "Esau ran. . .embraced. . .fell on his neck. . .kissed. . .wept" These are all signs of
a warm greeting.

- "ran," BDB 930, KB 1207, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

- "embraced," BDB 287, KB 287, Piel IMPERFECT with waw

- "fell on his neck," BDB 656, KB 709, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Gen. 45:14; 46:29

- "kissed," BDB 676, KB 730, Qal IMPERFECT with waw (this is missing in the LXX and
marked in the MT as an addition), cf. Gen. 45:15; 48:10; 50:1

- "they wept," BDB 13, KB 129, Qal IMPERFECT with waw (the LXX and TEV, REB have "they
both wept," but possibly, "he wept," cf. NJB, AB, p. 258)

The UBS Text Project, p. 50, gives "they" an "A" rating (high probability).

verses.zh: 以扫举目看见妇人孩子，就说：「这些和你同行的是谁呢？」雅各说：「这些孩子是　神施恩给你的仆人的。」
verses.en: When Esau[NOTE:1] looked up[NOTE:2] and saw the women and the children, he asked, “Who are these people with you?” Jacob[NOTE:3] replied, “The children whom God has graciously given[NOTE:4] your servant.”
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (Esau) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “lifted up his eyes.”
Heb “and he”; the referent (Jacob) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew verb means “to be gracious; to show favor”; here it carries the nuance “to give graciously.”
verses.commentary:
33:5 Esau asks about the groups of women and their children who were all accompanying Jacob. It must
have been unusual for a man to have two wives and two concubines and children with each or Esau would not
have asked. Esau's reaction to this is not recorded.

verses.zh: 于是两个使女和她们的孩子前来下拜；
verses.en: The female servants came forward with their children and bowed down.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the female servants drew near, they and their children and they bowed down.”

verses.zh: 利亚和她的孩子也前来下拜；随后约瑟和拉结也前来下拜。
verses.en: Then Leah came forward with her children and they bowed down. Finally Joseph and Rachel came forward and bowed down.

verses.zh: 以扫说：「我所遇见的这些群畜是甚么意思呢？」雅各说：「是要在我主面前蒙恩的。」
verses.en: Esau[NOTE:1] then asked, “What did you intend[NOTE:2] by sending all these herds to meet me?”[NOTE:3] Jacob[NOTE:4] replied, “To find favor in your sight, my lord.”
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (Esau) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Who to you?”
Heb “all this camp which I met.”
Heb “and he”; the referent (Jacob) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
33:8 Esau asks about all the presents (i.e., animals) that Jacob has sent before his family
(cf. Gen. 32:13-21).

verses.zh: 以扫说：「兄弟啊，我的已经够了，你的仍归你吧！」
verses.en: But Esau said, “I have plenty, my brother. Keep what belongs to you.”
verses.commentary:
33:9 "my brother" The NASB Study Bible (p. 51) makes a good point in mentioning that Esau calls Jacob
"my brother," but Jacob calls Esau "my lord." Jacob is either (1) being tactful or (2) fearful.

Gifts were common at special occasions. To refuse a gift in this culture implied a strained
relationship (i.e., James M. Freeman, Manners and Customs of the Bible, p. 41). Esau's refusal would
have supported Jacob's worst fears! Esau did not need these gifts, but accepted them as a sign of accepting
his brother.

verses.zh: 雅各说：「不然，我若在你眼前蒙恩，就求你从我手里收下这礼物；因为我见了你的面，如同见了　神的面，并且你容纳了我。
verses.en: “No, please take them,” Jacob said.[NOTE:1] “If I have found favor in your sight, accept[NOTE:2] my gift from my hand. Now that I have seen your face and you have accepted me,[NOTE:3] it is as if I have seen the face of God.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and Jacob said, ‘No, please.’” The words “take them” have been supplied in the translation for clarity, and the order of the introductory clause and the direct discourse rearranged for stylistic reasons.
The form is the perfect tense with a vav (ו) consecutive, expressing a contingent future nuance in the “then” section of the conditional sentence.
The verbal form is the preterite with a vav (ו) consecutive, indicating result here.

This is an allusion to the preceding episode (32:22-31) in which Jacob saw the face of God and realized his prayer was answered.tn Heb “for therefore I have seen your face like seeing the face of God and you have accepted me.”
verses.commentary:
33:10 Jacob urges Esau to accept his gifts because Esau's acceptance of him (cf. Gen. 33:14) would
parallel God's graciousness ("as one sees the face of God") toward him. This may be a veiled allusion to
Gen. 25:23.

verses.zh: 求你收下我带来给你的礼物；因为　神恩待我，使我充足。」雅各再三地求他，他才收下了。
verses.en: Please take my present[NOTE:1] that was brought to you, for God has been generous[NOTE:2] to me and I have all I need.”[NOTE:3] When Jacob urged him, he took it.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “blessing.” It is as if Jacob is trying to repay what he stole from his brother twenty years earlier.
Or “gracious,” but in the specific sense of prosperity.
Heb “all.”
Heb “and he urged him and he took.” The referent of the first pronoun in the sequence (“he”) has been specified as “Jacob” in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
33:11 Jacob acknowledges the source of his physical wealth as the covenant God (i.e., "graciously,"
BDB 335, KB 334, Qal PERFECT, cf. Gen. 33:5; 43:29).

▣ "gift" This (BDB 139) is literally "blessing." It is the very term used to describe what
Jacob cheated Esau of in chapter 27. It is not by accident that Jacob wants to bless his brother by giving
a gift (lit. blessing). In a sense he was trying to make up for his earlier manipulations.

verses.zh: 以扫说：「我们可以起身前往，我在你前头走。」
verses.en: Then Esau[NOTE:1] said, “Let’s be on our way![NOTE:2] I will go in front of you.”
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (Esau) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “let us travel and let us go.” The two cohortatives are used in combination with the sense, “let’s travel along, get going, be on our way.”

verses.zh: 雅各对他说：「我主知道孩子们年幼娇嫩，牛羊也正在乳养的时候，若是催赶一天，群畜都必死了。
verses.en: But Jacob[NOTE:1] said to him, “My lord knows that the children are young,[NOTE:2] and that I have to look after the sheep and cattle that are nursing their young.[NOTE:3] If they are driven too hard for even a single day, all the animals will die.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Jacob) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “weak.”
Heb “and the sheep and the cattle nursing [are] upon me.”
verses.commentary:
33:13 One wonders if this was another way for Jacob to make Esau feel superior, as well as an excuse
for not traveling with him back to Seir immediately. His children were not "weak" and the flocks had already
traveled a long way. Is Jacob still a manipulative liar?

verses.zh: 求我主在仆人前头走，我要量着在我面前群畜和孩子的力量慢慢地前行，直走到西珥我主那里。」
verses.en: Let my lord go on ahead of his servant. I will travel more slowly, at the pace of the herds and the children,[NOTE:1] until I come to my lord at Seir.”
notes: Heb “and I, I will move along according to my leisure at the foot of the property which is before me and at the foot of the children.”

verses.zh: 以扫说：「容我把跟随我的人留几个在你这里。」雅各说：「何必呢？只要在我主眼前蒙恩就是了。」
verses.en: So Esau said, “Let me leave some of my men with you.”[NOTE:1] “Why do that?” Jacob replied.[NOTE:2] “My lord has already been kind enough to me.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The cohortative verbal form here indicates a polite offer of help.

Heb “and he said, ‘Why this?’” The referent of the pronoun “he” (Jacob) has been specified for clarity, and the order of the introductory clause and the direct discourse has been rearranged in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “I am finding favor in the eyes of my lord.”
verses.commentary:
33:15 "people" This is the term goi (BDB 766 I), which usually has a negative connotation
referring to Gentiles, but here it is used of Esau's men and in Exod. 33:13 it refers to the people of God.
Context, context, context determines word meaning, not lexicons! Words have meaning only in sentences;
sentences have meaning only in paragraphs/strophe or stanzas; and these have meaning only in larger literary
units. Be careful of "set" or "technical" definitions!

verses.zh: 于是，以扫当日起行，回往西珥去了。
verses.en: So that same day Esau made his way back[NOTE:1] to Seir.
notes: Heb “returned on his way.”

verses.zh: 雅各就往疏割去，在那里为自己盖造房屋，又为牲畜搭棚；因此那地方名叫疏割（就是棚的意思）。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] Jacob traveled to Sukkoth[NOTE:2] where he built himself a house and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place was called[NOTE:3] Sukkoth.[NOTE:4]
notes: The disjunctive clause contrasts Jacob’s action with Esau’s.

But Jacob traveled to Sukkoth. There are several reasons why Jacob chose not to go to Mt. Seir after Esau. First, as he said, his herds and children probably could not keep up with the warriors. Second, he probably did not fully trust his brother. The current friendliness could change, and he could lose everything. And third, God did tell him to return to his land, not Seir. But Jacob is still not able to deal truthfully, probably because of fear of Esau.
Heb “why he called.” One could understand “Jacob” as the subject of the verb, but it is more likely that the subject is indefinite, in which case the verb is better translated as passive.
The name Sukkoth means “shelters,” an appropriate name in light of the shelters Jacob built there for his livestock.
verses.commentary:
33:17 "Succoth" This term (BDB 697) means "booths." Jacob built a shelter for himself, but this is
called a "house" (BDB 108), but note Gen. 33:19. He also built "booths" (BDB 697, i.e., a shelter made
from branches) for his animals.

It is uncertain if there was a village in this area before Jacob camped there. It will later
become the name of a city (cf. Jdgs. 8:5).

This is not the same as the Succoth located in the Egyptian delta
(cf. Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5). This is a city on the east side of the Jordan (i.e., The MacMillan Bible
Atlas, p. 22).

One more point, Jacob does not seem to follow Esau to Mt. Seir, but travels to Succoth,
which is not on the way to Seir/Edom. He even builds a house! It is uncertain if the text is telling us
that (1) this was purposeful or (2) simply omits Jacob's visit to Seir. I prefer option #2. I want to
believe Jacob has truly changed, that he is no longer the trickster, manipulator, liar.

verses.zh: 雅各从巴旦・亚兰回来的时候，平平安安地到了迦南地的示剑城，在城东支搭帐棚，
verses.en: After he left Paddan Aram, Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and he camped near[NOTE:1] the city.
notes: Heb “in front of.”
verses.commentary:
33:18 "Shechem" The name can refer to

- a person's name, Gen. 33:18,19; 34:2; Num. 26:31; Jos. 17:2; 24:32; Jdg. 9:28

- a topological region between Mt. Ebal and Mt. Gerazim. The same root (BDB 1014 I) means
"shoulder" or "shoulder-blade."

- a city, Jos. 20:7; 21:21; 24:1; Jdg. 8:31

It is first mentioned in Gen. 12:6 in connection with Abram and now with Jacob (cf. Gen. 37:14).

There is no apparent connection between Gen. 33:17 and Gen. 33:18. How long Jacob stayed
at Succoth is not recorded. They seem to be two separate events and times recorded with no clear connection.
From building a house to buying land may imply temporary to permanent residence. The only problem is that
Gen. 33:18 seems to imply soon after Jacob arrived from Paddan-aram (area around Haran) he bought the land.

He was told to return to Bethel, but he stopped short and remained. Why is not stated in the
text!

verses.zh: 就用一百块银子向示剑的父亲、哈抹的子孙买了支帐棚的那块地，
verses.en: Then he purchased the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent; he bought it[NOTE:1] from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for 100 pieces of money.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “he bought it” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text v. 19 is one long sentence.
The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (qesitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value is unknown. (However, cf. REB, which renders the term as “sheep”).
verses.commentary:
33:19 "He bought the piece of land where he had pitched his tent" The act of buying a field implied
residency or at least shows legal residency.

▣ "Hamor" This name means "ass" (BDB 331 II). In the ancient world donkeys were considered
sacred animals. We know this, not only from the Mari Tablets, but also from the fact that

- the wealthy rode donkeys (cf. Jdgs. 5:10)

- Israel's kings rode on a special donkey for their royal mount (i.e., 1 Kgs. 1:33)

▣ "for one hundred pieces of money" This is a rare Hebrew term,
קשׂיטה, qesitah (BDB 903). It is an unknown weight of metal
(cf. Jos. 24:32; Job 42:11), possibly

- the price of a lamb (LXX)

- a weight (mina) of metal in the shape (or imprint) of a lamb

verses.zh: 在那里筑了一座坛，起名叫伊利・伊罗伊・以色列（就是　神、以色列　神的意思）。
verses.en: There he set up an altar and called it “The God of Israel is God.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “God, the God of Israel.” Rather than translating the name, a number of modern translations merely transliterate it from the Hebrew as “El Elohe Israel” (cf. NIV, NRSV, REB). It is not entirely clear how the name should be interpreted grammatically. One option is to supply an equative verb, as in the translation: “The God of Israel [is] God.” Another interpretive option is “the God of Israel [is] strong [or “mighty”].” Buying the land and settling down for a while was a momentous step for the patriarch, so the commemorative naming of the altar is significant.
verses.commentary:
33:20 "he erected there an altar" This designated a place, time, and manner of worshiping. It allowed
prayer and sacrifice to be offered to YHWH (cf. Gen. 8:20; 12:7-8; 13:18; 22:9; 26:25). This is a fulfillment
of YHWH's promise of Gen. 28:15!

The IVP Bible Background Commentary, p. 66, has a good comment on v. 20.

"Altars function as sacrificial platforms. Their construction can also mark the introduction
of the worship of a particular god in a new land. One tie between the generations of covenantal leaders
is their construction of altars in order to worship Yahweh in the Promised Land (12:7-8; 13:18; 26:25). The
name given to Jacob/Israel's altar, 'El Elohe Israel,' is an acknowledgment of his own name change and his
acceptance of the role of covenantal heir that had been promised at Bethel (28:13-15). For another example
of naming an altar, see Exodus 17:15."

▣ "El-Elohe-Israel" This CONSTRUCT is made up of

- El, BDB 42, cf. Exod. 34:6; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES
FOR DEITY, A.

- Elohe, BDB 43, cf. Deut. 32:15,17; Ps. 18:32

- Israel, see SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL
(THE NAME)

The Septuagint translates it as "the God of Israel." The Jewish Study Bible, using the JPSOA
translation in its textual footnote, has "El, God of Israel" (p. 69).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter includes mostly dialogue (note TEV translation). The term "say" (BDB 55, KB 65) is
used ten times. This dialogue format has several commands/requests.

- "let what you have be your own," Gen. 33:9, BDB 224, KB 243, Qal JUSSIVE

- "please take my gifts," Gen. 33:11 BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "let us take our journey," Gen. 33:12, BDB 652, KB 704, Qal COHORTATIVE

- "go" (twice), Gen. 33:12, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal COHORTATIVE

- same as #4

- "please let my lord pass on before his servant," Gen. 33:14, BDB 716, KB 778, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "I will proceed at my leisure," Gen. 33:14, BDB 624, KB 675, Hithpael
COHORTATIVE

- "please let me leave with you some of my people who are with me," Gen. 33:15, BDb 426,
KB 427, Hiphil COHORTATIVE

- "let me find favor in the sight of my lord," Gen. 33:15, BDB 592, KB 619, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- Jacob has faced his fears.

- Laban

- the angelic wrestler

- Esau

- Jacob is back in the Promised Land (Canaan). The divine promises of Bethel have been fulfilled.
The covenant promises to Abraham and his seed continue (i.e., the eternal redemptive plan is on
track).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 33:1-3

1Then Jacob lifted his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and four hundred men with him. So he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two maids. 2He put the maids and their children in front, and Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph last. 3But he himself passed on ahead of them and bowed down to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
